question.leadin: The Balfour Declaration supported the creation of a "national home" for members of a certain religion, which became this country.
question.text: Name this country that was invaded by five Arab nations shortly after its creation in 1948.
question.clue: Along with Lehi , another paramilitary group carried out the Deir Yassin massacre in this modern-day country, although the Haganah criticized them for violating this country's "purity of arms" policy.

swap.leadin: In July 1990, this country was accused of slant drilling into the Rumaila oil field; a month later, this country was invaded.
swap.text: Name this Middle Eastern country. American forces supported this occupied country during the First Gulf War.
swap.clue: This nation lacks any permanent rivers, and depends on desalination plants to provide drinking water for its inhabitants.

question.leadin: In the weeks after this man was overthrown in a July 3, 2013 military coup, he was said to be in a "safe place" but had not made a public appearance.
question.text: Name this former President of the Muslim Brotherhood's political party, the Freedom and Justice Party, who was elected President of his nation in 2012, shortly after the downfall of Hosni Mubarak.
question.clue: This leader defeated the Salafist Nour party to win his first election.

swap.text: This computer worm attacked Iran's Natanz uranium enrichment facilities and was the first discovered malware to subvert industrial systems.
swap.clue: This computer virus, likely sponsored by the United States and Israel, targeted Iran's nuclear program. This virus placed a rootkit on programmable logical controllers, ultimately destroying one-fifth of Iran's nuclear centrifuges.

question.text: The Battle of the Eclipse was fought over the Halys River in this present-day country. Heinrich Schliemann explored ruins in this modern-day country near the town of Hisarlik.
question.clue: A region in this modern-day country contained the city of Hattusa, home to a Bronze Age civilization that mastered ironworking and was ruled by Muwatalli II.

swap.text: This modern Iraqi city was the location where the Barmakid family used the prisoners from the Battle of Talas to discover papermaking. This city was the capital of the Abbasid Caliphate and contained the House of Wisdom.
swap.clue: This city was founded by al-Mansur and contained the House of Wisdom, a key institute in the Islamic Golden Age.

question.leadin: Sometimes leaving no choice but going through your enemies leads to victory.
question.text: Tariq ibn Ziyad captured Hispania for this Islamic caliphate after forcing his soldiers to burn their ships.
question.clue: This empire was overthrown after the Battle of the Zab but persisted in Al-Andalus as the Caliphate of Cordoba.

swap.leadin: An invasion plan during this war had its name changed after the British and the French couldn't agree on how to spell the word "Hamilcar."
swap.text: Name this brief conflict. Lester Pearson received a Nobel Peace Prize for his work in ending it.
swap.answerHtml: Suez Crisis [or Suez War; or Suez Canal Crisis; or Suez Canal War; or the Tripartite Aggression; or Second Arab-Israeli War]
swap.clue: This conflict was the center of discussions at the Protocol of Sevres after which Charles Keightley initiated Operation Musketeer.

question.leadin: BONUS. Answer the following about 1967 per part.
question.text: This conflict saw Israeli forces take the old city of Jerusalem.
question.clue: A major cause of this non-Suez Crisis war was the blockade of Eilat, and this war began with the surprise Operation Focus, which destroyed most of Egypt's air force while it was on the ground.

swap.leadin: Da'wah missions sent by this caliphate's ruler al-Moezz converted many people in Khorasan ("CORE-uh-sahn") to Isma'ilism.
swap.text: Name this Shi'a caliphate which ruled Egypt from the 10th through 12th centuries.
swap.clue: That "mad" ruler from this dynasty, al-Hakim, mysteriously disappeared on one of his meditative night walks and is venerated by the Druze.

question.text: The Battle of Basian was part of Tamar's expansionist campaigns against an empire ruled by this dynasty. The vizier Nizam al-Mulk helped this dynasty's ruler Alp Arslan invade and subjugate Georgia in the late 11th century.
question.clue: One offshoot of this dynastic group was the Sultanate of Rum.

swap.leadin: This man told the captured Romanos IV Diogenes that he would punish the other man by forgiving him and setting him free.
swap.text: Name this monarch who decisively defeated the Byzantine Empire at the 1071 Battle of Manzikert.
swap.clue: According to Edward Gibbon, this man died when he waved his bodyguards away and tried to shoot an assassin with his own bow.

question.leadin: During a battle, a general of these people flung off his helmet and yelled "oh my Islam" to prevent the enemy escaping from one side of the battle.
question.text: Name this state, whose ruler Qutuz was assassinated shortly after winning a battle against a seemingly unstoppable Ilkhanate in 1260.

swap.text: Fatimah, the daughter of this Sunni theologian, is also known for her dedication to women's education as part of Islamic reform. This theologian founded a namesake religious movement adopted by Muhammad bin Saud.
swap.answerHtml: Muḥammad ibn ‘Abd al-Wahhāb [or Muḥammad ibn ‘Abd al-Wahhāb ibn Sulaymān al-Tamīmī; accept Wahhabi movement or Wahhabism or Wahhabiyya]
swap.clue: In his hometown of Uyaynah, he gained the favor of a ruler named Uthman, whom he directed to begin a campaign of iconoclasm, destroying the domes on the gravesites of Muhammad's companion.

question.leadin: This man attempted to catch a pair of shoes thrown at George W. Bush during a press conference.
question.text: Name this former Prime Minister of Iraq whose accession was brokered by Qasem Soleimani as a compromise between Kurds and Shi'ites.

swap.leadin: After bulldozing some berms upon capturing Mosul, ISIS claimed to have ended this agreement.
swap.text: Name this agreement, named for the British and French officials who created it, by which France and the U.K. partitioned the Middle East.
swap.clue: British control over Palestine was decided in this secret 1916 agreement between Britain and France that divided up the territories of the Ottoman Empire.

question.text: Later, the Umayyads faced the Great Berber Revolt in the 740s, inspired by preachers from this sect. One of this sect's members killed Ali, even though they allied with Ali against the Umayyads during the First Fitna.
question.clue: Once selected as Caliph, Ali faced several revolts during the First Fitna, including by this breakaway sect which Ali defeated at the Battle of Nahrawan.

swap.leadin: A Latin maxim beginning with the phrase "sit tibi copia" is inscribed in Rayonnant ("RYE-yoh-NAHN") Gothic style on the portico of this structure's great Gothic hall.
swap.text: Name this structure originally built for the Mirdasid dynasty. T.E. Lawrence wrote that it was the "the best preserved and most wholly admirable" structure of its kind in the world.
swap.answerHtml: Krak des Chevaliers (“krahk day shev-ah-L’YAY”) [or Crac de l’Hospital or Hisn al-Akrād; prompt on Krak; reject “Kerak”]
swap.clue: Speaking of Baybars, in 1271 CE, he successfully launched a siege against this Crusader castle near Homs which had been built up by the Knights Hospitallers starting in 1140 CE under direction of Raymond II, Count of Tripoli.

question.leadin: Answer the following about some Middle Eastern events that happened in 1990.
question.text: In 1990, Saddam Hussein sent his army on this campaign, which successfully brought rich oil fields under Hussein's control. It was the major impetus for the Gulf War.
question.answerHtml: the Iraqi invasion of Kuwait [in place of “invasion,” accept: obvious equivalents]
question.clue: The aggressor in this event accused its neighbor of cross drilling into the Rumaila Oil Field.

swap.leadin: Mur ad-Din ruled from this city that had a famous Citadel in which Joscelin II was held captive.
swap.text: Name this city, an emirate under Seljuk rule that was sacked by Tamarlane in 1400 and also contains a Great Mosque.
swap.clue: A rebuilt version of the Ayyubid Palace of Glory is contained within a defensive structure used by Seleucus Nicator, this massive Citadel of this city, outside of which Tamerlane built a tower of 20,000 skulls after taking it from the Mamluks.
